title: Classical finite-coefficient complexes in the supported hull, with integral scalar restriction
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a qcqs scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. All sites and diagrams are small in the fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(R,B)$ be either $(B,B)$ for a finite discrete commutative ring $B$ killed by a power of $\ell$, with identity coefficient map, or $(O,O/\pi^n)$ for $O=\mathcal O_F$, $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $n\geq1$, and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. In the second case give $O$ its valuation topology and $B$ its finite discrete topology. Use the actual condensed rings $R^c(P)=C(P,R)$, $B^c(P)=C(P,B)$, the canonical quotient map, and their pulled-back ring objects $R_T,B_T$ [sk-def-localizing-closure, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}	o T_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ be site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For every $C\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{\acute et}},B)$, interpret $
u_T^*C$ as an internal $B_T$-module derived object by the finite discrete coefficient equivalence [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence]. Then its exact derived scalar restriction satisfies
$$\operatorname{Res}_{R_T	o B_T}(
u_T^*C)\in\mathcal G_T(R^c).$$
Here derived restriction is the termwise restriction of scalars of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], exact by its clause 4 and hence well defined on derived categories; it is the identity in the first case. The class $\mathcal G_T(R^c)$ is exactly the ordinary uncompleted supported model hull [def-sfb-supported-model-hull]: supported finitely presented scalar local models, zero, shifts, triangle extensions, retracts, small derived products and strict filtered complex colimits with a common termwise lower bound. No constructibility, finite generation, Tor-amplitude or cohomological upper bound is required of $C$. No Noetherianity of $T$, characteristic or invertibility-of-$\ell$ hypothesis is imposed. Empty $T$, $C=0$, nonreduced finite rings and torsion scalar modules are included.

proof.text: First verify the local scalar calculation, on any scheme $W$. A finite $B$-module $P$ has a finite presentation: take its finitely many elements as generators and all addition and scalar-action relations as a finite generating set of relations. For $R=B$, the finite-discrete scalar-model comparison identifies its constant sheaf with $B_W\otimes_{\underline B}\underline P$. For $R=O$, lift a presentation $B^s\xrightarrow{A}B^r\to P\to0$ to a matrix $\widetilde A$ over $O$ and put $D=(\widetilde A,\pi^n I_r):O^{s+r}\to O^r$. Reduction modulo $\pi^n$ identifies $\operatorname{coker}D$ with $P$, now as an $O$-module. Right exact scalar extension identifies $O_W\otimes_{\underline O}\underline P$ with $\operatorname{coker}D_W$. The actual quotient isomorphism $O_W/\pi^nO_W\cong B_W$ from integral quotient normalization identifies this cokernel with the constant $P$ sheaf restricted along the prescribed quotient $O_W\to B_W$. Thus restriction of a finite constant $B$-model is a finite constant scalar $R$-model. The internal/section scalar comparison ensures this uses the actual scalar action, not an abstract identification of underlying abelian sheaves.

source.place: Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat, canonical quotient clause; finite presentation calculation over that quotient

proof.text: Let $F$ be a constructible étale $B$-module sheaf on $T$, and put $M=\operatorname{Res}(\nu_T^*F)$. Finite-ring constructible comparison gives a finite constructible locally closed partition of $T$ on which $\nu_T^*F$ is locally constant with finite $B$-module values. The ordinary/internal finite-coefficient equivalence and the finite-discrete scalar-model comparison identify these constant values with finite scalar models. On every trivializing cover, step 1 identifies their scalar restrictions with finite scalar $R$-models. Pullback commutes with scalar restriction here: both underlying sheaves are inverse images of the same abelian sheaf, and their actions are the composites of the pulled-back quotient with the pulled-back $B$-action; the cartesian coefficient identifications give the same composites. Hence $M$ is constructible in the finite constant scalar-model sense on that same partition. No local freeness of $P$ is used.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible, and Tag 099Y, lemma-compare-locally-constant; apply the preceding scalar calculation

proof.text: Apply the finite constant-local-model tree theorem to the one-element family consisting of $M$. Its hypotheses are qcqs $T$ and precisely the constructibility just proved. It supplies a finite qcqs open-closed tree such that the actual leaf restrictions $p^*M$ are finite scalar local models. Each open edge is quasi-compact and each closed edge has the complementary quasi-compact open edge, so every path is a support chain allowed in the hull definition. In particular the refinement does not use Noetherian induction or replace scheme-theoretic pullbacks by set containment.

source.place: Tag 09Y4, lemma-constructible-partition-refined-by-stratification, in its existing scheme-theoretic tree formulation

proof.text: Fix any class $\mathscr P$ occurring in the defining intersection for $\mathcal G_T(R^c)$. At a vertex $V$ let $J_V$ be its exact extension along the path to $T$. At a leaf $W$, $J_W(p_W^*M)[0]$ is a supported generator, hence belongs to $\mathscr P$. For an internal vertex with children $j:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$, use the short exact sequence $0\to j_!j^*(M|_V)\to M|_V\to i_*i^*(M|_V)\to0$. Internal/section operation comparison identifies these operations with those of the hull. Both edge extensions are exact, so $J_V$ is exact; applying it and then the short-exact-sequence triangle theorem gives a triangle whose outside terms are the two child objects. Induction on the finite number of vertices and extension closure of $\mathscr P$ put $M[0]$ in $\mathscr P$ at the root. Since $\mathscr P$ was arbitrary, every restricted constructible $F[0]$ lies in $\mathcal G_T(R^c)$. Empty leaves have the zero model and cause no exception.

proof.text: Write $E=\operatorname{Res}\circ\nu_T^*$, including the internal finite-coefficient equivalence. Its factors are additive exact functors, so it induces a triangulated functor on ordinary derived categories and $H^q(EK)\cong E(H^qK)$. By step 5 every $E(H^qK)[0]$ lies in the hull. Shift closure and the bounded degreewise dévissage theorem therefore show that $E(K)$ lies in the hull whenever $K$ has cohomology in a finite interval: take the property $Q$ there to be hull membership and each $P_q$ to mean being of the form $E(F)$ for an étale $B$-module $F$. The zero interval uses the zero object. This is an induction on the length of the interval, using the canonical truncation triangles, and assumes neither finite Tor amplitude nor constructibility of the cohomology.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, finite induction; exact functor comparison is homology.tex Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor

proof.text: Finally choose a representative $K$ of $C$ with $K^q=0$ for $q<a$, using the standard t-structure description of $D^+$. For $m=a,a+1,\ldots$, take its good upper subcomplex $K_m=\tau_{\leq m}K$, with term $\ker(d^m)$ in degree $m$, zero above $m$, and the terms of $K$ below $m$. The natural inclusions $K_m\to K_{m+1}$ form a strict sequence. Every $K_m$ has finite cohomological interval $[a,m]$, so $Q(EK_m)$ is in the hull by step 6. All $EK_m$ vanish termwise below $a$. For any fixed degree $q$, once $m>q$ its terms and transition maps are exactly $E(K^q)$ and the identity; its colimit is $E(K^q)$. These identifications commute with differentials since every fixed adjacent pair also stabilizes. Equivalently, a compatible cocone determines its unique map from $EK$ by its stabilized components. Thus $\varinjlim_m EK_m=EK$ termwise, without invoking an exchange of inverse limits or unbounded derived colimits. The strict filtered-colimit clause of the hull, with lower bound $a$, gives $Q(EK)\in\mathcal G_T(R^c)$. Repleteness transports this along the chosen representative isomorphism to $E(C)$, the asserted object.
